explanation: The statement is about the library-local ring hom `locHom φ z : X.presheaf.stalk z →+* F`, defined as `φ.symm.comp (algebraMap (stalk z) X.functionField)`; Mathlib knows nothing of `locHom` (nor of `SemistableModel`), and indeed no Mathlib declaration is stated in these terms. I searched Mathlib for a lemma internalising the compatibility used here — i.e. that `algebraMap (stalk z₁) X.functionField ∘ stalkSpecializes h = algebraMap (stalk z₂) X.functionField`, which is the mathematical content: greps for `stalkSpecializes` throughout Mathlib (Topology/Sheaves/Stalks.lean, Geometry/RingedSpace/*, AlgebraicGeometry/Scheme.lean, FunctionField.lean, Stalk.lean, ValuativeCriterion.lean, SpreadingOut.lean) and for `algebraMap`/`functionField` combinations with `stalkSpecializes` turn up only `TopCat.Presheaf.stalkSpecializes_comp`, `germ_stalkSpecializes`, `stalkSpecializes_stalkMap`, etc. The only occurrence tying the function-field algebra structure to `stalkSpecializes` is the instance definition `Scheme.stalkFunctionFieldAlgebra` (FunctionField.lean:81–85). Hence the theorem's content lives in the library's own definition of `locHom`, and there is no single Mathlib declaration asserting it.
